payload.claim: `tree_base = stacked_on if stacked_on is not None else base.base_sha` re-derives, as a second local computation, exactly what `CellSpec.tree_base` (saffron/cell/session.py:292-301) already computes and whose docstring states is 'one name for the second base, so no consumer picks its own — the defect this field exists to remove is two things sharing one word, and a second word every caller resolves separately is the same bug.' This diff adds exactly that second word: a caller (run_task) now resolves stacked_on-vs-base_sha itself instead of reading it off the CellSpec once built. It happens to agree with the property today because both read the same two inputs, but the documented contract was that this resolution has exactly one site, and this diff creates a second one that can silently drift from the property's definition on a future change to either.
